//! The lowering rule of a block: a scope of its own holding its statements, its value its tail's.
use core.{ExprId, Lowering, Lowers, Reg, owned_type}
use core.expr.{Block}

impl Lowers for Block {
    /// A block's value is lifted where the block stands, so its tail is read as it's born.
    /// A block holding only its value is that value. Any other is a scope: its statements in order,
    /// then its tail's value, or where it ends in a statement, nothing of the type it ends as: the
    /// fn's answer where it leaves, else `void`.
    fn lowered(mut cx: Lowering, e: ExprId) -> Reg {
        let lead = cx.store.lead_of(e)
        let tail = cx.store.tail_of(e)
        if lead.is_empty() && tail != null { return cx.born(tail!) }

        cx.closed_giving(r)
        cx.scope_exit(r)
        r
    }

    }

// proves: a task a `select` arm's head makes belongs to the `select`: leaving
// it by another arm cancels each one still running — a lone task, each member
// of a list written in the head, a second head, and under an arm whose body
// returns — while the taken arm's own task answers, in both engines alike
use @std.time.{after, ms, sleep}

fn slow(left: Cell<string>, name: string, span: int) -> int {
    defer left.set(left.get() + "${name}-left ")
    sleep(ms(span))
    left.set(left.get() + "${name}-done ")
    1
}

fn by_timer(left: Cell<string>) -> int {
    let limit = after(ms(20))
    select {
        r in spawn slow(left, "a", 900) -> r
        limit -> 0 - 1
    }
}

fn by_list(left: Cell<string>) -> int {
    let limit = after(ms(20))
    select {
        r in [spawn slow(left, "b", 900), spawn slow(left, "c", 900)] -> r
        limit -> 0 - 1
    }
}

fn by_task(left: Cell<string>) -> int {
    select {
        r in spawn slow(left, "d", 10) -> r
        r in spawn slow(left, "e", 900) -> r + 10
    }
}

fn returning(left: Cell<string>) -> int {
    let limit = after(ms(20))

TASKS IN ARM HEADS. A task made by an arm's expression belongs to the
`select`. Leaving the `select` cancels each one not taken (an offer is
retracted, a timer dropped). It is never joined. (v2 would have waited
out every unfired `quiet`.)

TIMERS, BY TYPE. `after(d)` answers `Deadline`; `quiet(d)` answers
`Quiet`. An arm whose head is a CALL answering `Deadline`, inside a
loop, is `flow.fresh_deadline`: it would restart every turn. `Quiet`
is the type that says so on purpose. The rule reads types, never names.

# list's parts share its weight in turn
dealt() { awk -v k="$1" -v n="$2" '(NR - 1) % n == k'; }

# `test` over `$2…` as the row `$1`, judged by the NAMES that fail: each must be one
# tools/gate/<package>.names pins (a case a sandbox's environment fails — root writes any directory, no
# terminal, no network), never a count. With no pin file, every failure fails the row.
# A CASE THAT ENDS THE SUITE'S PROCESS (`avra: while running <case>`) fails no case by name and leaves
# every case after it unrun, so it is never passed over: each must be one tools/gate/<package>.traps
# lists, by the first line the runner says it under.
tested() {
    name=$1; shift
    pkg=$(echo "$1" | cut -d/ -f2)
    sh tools/bounded.sh "$ROW_SECS" build/avra test "$@" >"$out/$name.log" 2>&1
    ran=$?
    grep '^    ✗' "$out/$name.log" | sed 's/ @ .*//; s/^    ✗ //' | sort -u >"$out/$name.failed"
    listed "tools/gate/$pkg.names" >"$out/$name.known"
    comm -23 "$out/$name.failed" "$out/$name.known" >"$out/$name.unpinned"
    grep '^avra: while running ' "$out/$name.log" | sed 's/ @ .*//; s/^avra: while running //' | sort -u >"$out/$name.trapped"
    listed "tools/gate/$pkg.traps" >"$out/$name.traps"
    comm -23 "$out/$name.trapped" "$out/$name.traps" >"$out/$name.untrapped"
    if [ -s "$out/$name.untrapped" ]; then judged "$name" "$(wc -l <"$out/$name.untrapped" | tr -d ' ')"; return; fi

# every store under the packages named emptied — a nested package's and a program test's too — so the
# rows after read them cold
cold() { for p in "$@"; do find "packages/$p" -name .avra-cache -prune -exec find {} -delete \; ; done; return 0; }

# build/avra as HEAD's compiler: kept when it was built from this tree's compiler source, else made in
# ONE generation — from the committed seed's link where no compiler stands, else from the one that does
# — with the package libraries beside it, built without building the compiler again. A gate's
# compiler makes no claim of the net, so it is built without it; the two-generation fixed point is the
# build slice's.
compiler() {
    if compiler_stands; then return 0; fi
    if [ ! -x build/avra ]; then row compiler-recover make recover || return 1; fi
    row compiler-gen1 env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make avra || return 1
    row compiler-libs env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make -o avra libs
}

# what `$1`'s cold build of packages/cli took, in seconds, net on or off by `$2`
cli_built() {
    cold cli
    find "$AVRA_CACHE_DIR" -mindepth 1 -delete
    c0=$(date +%s)
    row "cli-build-$1-cold" env -u AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli || return 1
    c1=$(date +%s)
    row "cli-build-$1-warm" env -u AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli || return 1
    echo "cli build net $1: cold $((c1 - c0))s, warm $(( $(date +%s) - c1 ))s" >>"$out/seconds"
    # the warm build's heir waited out, before a row after empties the store it saves
    env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
}

slice_build() {
    row try make try
    row avra-a make avra && cp build/avra "$out/avra-a"
    cold cli

//! WHAT A DECLARATION LEAVES OUT ON PURPOSE: `@std/meta`'s `@lacks(field, why)` marks a record, each
//! field once and never one the record declares; an enum has no fields to lack. Read off the marks
//! the file's declarations wear and the record's signature.
use core.{Span}
use compiler.laws.{Found, law}
use compiler.typing.{lacks_declared_said, lacks_on_enum_said, lacks_twice_said}
use diagnostics.{Voice}
use @std.program.address.{SourceFileAddress}
use @std.program.query_engine.{QueryEngine}

/// The mark a declaration wears to leave a field out.
const LACKS: string = "lacks"

/// A declaration the written item `at` of `file` makes wearing `@lacks`: its name, its kind, where it
/// stands, and each field a mark names, in the order they're worn.
type Lacking = { name: string, kind: ItemKind, at: Span?, fields: List<string> }

fn lacking_at(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<Lacking> {
    let worn = [m for m in file_marks(engine, file).worn if m.item == at && m.mark == LACKS]
    if worn.is_empty() || !meta_marker(engine, file, LACKS) { return [] }
    let item = read_item(engine, file, at)
    [Lacking { name: d.name, kind: d.kind, at: declared_place(item, d.name), fields: fs } for d in file_declares_at(engine, file, at).names if d.item == at for fs in [[f! for m in worn if m.name == d.name for f in [lacked_field(m)] if f != null]] if !fs.is_empty()]
}

/// The field a `@lacks` mark names: its first of exactly two literals, where that's text.
fn lacked_field(m: WornMark) -> string? {
    let ls? = m.literals else { return null }
    if ls.length != 2 { return null }
    match ls[0] { .Text(t) -> t, rest -> null }
}

/// Where the declaration `name` the item `item` makes stands.
fn declared_place(item: ReadItem, name: string) -> Span? {
    let s? = item.stmts.find((st) -> item.store.declared_name(st) == name) else { return null }
    item.store.stmt_span(s)
}

/// Every enum the written item `at` of `file` declares wearing `@lacks`, where it stands.
fn enums_lacking(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<Found> {
    [Found { at: l.at, args: [] } for l in lacking_at(engine, file, at) if l.kind == ItemKind.Enum]
}

/// Every `@lacks` a record the written item `at` of `file` declares wears over a field it declares:
/// where the record stands, the record, the field.
fn lacked_declared(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<Found> {
    [Found { at: l.at, args: [l.name, f] } for l in lacking_at(engine, file, at) if l.kind == ItemKind.Record for names in [[x.name for x in record_signature(engine, file, l.name)?.fields ?? []]] for f in l.fields if names.contains(f)]
}

/// Every `@lacks` a record the written item `at` of `file` declares wears over a field an earlier one
/// names: where the record stands, the record, the field.
fn lacked_twice(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<Found> {
    [Found { at: l.at, args: [l.name, f] } for l in lacking_at(engine, file, at) if l.kind == ItemKind.Record for j, f in l.fields if l.fields.take(j).contains(f)]
}

/// only a record lacks a field
export law lacks_on_a_record {
    kind: "type.lacks"
    reads: enums_lacking
    voice: enum_words
    witness: "use @std.meta.{lacks}\n\n@lacks(\"x\", \"why\")\nenum K { A, B }\n"
}

/// a record lacks no field it declares
export law lacks_undeclared {
    kind: "type.lacks"
    reads: lacked_declared
    voice: declared_words
    witness: "use @std.meta.{lacks}\n\n@lacks(\"a\", \"why\")\ntype P = { a: int }\n"
}

/// a record lacks each field once
export law lacks_once {
    kind: "type.lacks"
    reads: lacked_twice
    voice: twice_words
    witness: "use @std.meta.{lacks}\n\n@lacks(\"x\", \"first\")\n@lacks(\"x\", \"second\")\ntype P = { a: int }\n"
}

fn enum_words(_a: List<string>) -> Voice { lacks_on_enum_said() }

fn declared_words(a: List<string>) -> Voice { lacks_declared_said(a[0], a[1]) }

fn twice_words(a: List<string>) -> Voice { lacks_twice_said(a[0], a[1]) }
EOF

new='''    fn enum_lacks(s: StmtId) { self.emit(said_as("type.lacks", self.stmt_loc(s), lacks_on_enum_said())) }

//! WHERE A FN LOWERED AT ITS CALL IS READ AS A VALUE: `@std/meta`'s `embed` and `provided` read a
//! file their call's literal names, and `guarded` is lowered around the body its call writes, so a
//! bare read of one — bound, handed to a seat, anywhere but called — is refused, said at the read.
//! Read off the names a body's typing resolved to no binding of its own.
use core.{ExprId, NameRead, SyntaxArena, flatten}
use compiler.laws.{Found, law}
use diagnostics.{Voice}
use features.{embed_uncalled, guard_uncalled}
use @std.program.address.{SourceFileAddress}
use @std.program.query_engine.{QueryEngine}

/// The package declaring the fns lowered where they're called.
const CALLED_META: string = "@std/meta"

/// Every bare read in the written item `at` of `file` of a fn among `words` that `@std/meta`
/// declares, where it's read.
fn meta_values(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int, words: List<string>) -> List<Found> {
    if !item_held(engine, file, at) { return [] }
    let item = read_item(engine, file, at)
    if !item.store.refusals().is_empty() { return [] }
    let own = flatten(
        [metas_read(engine, file, item.store, b.reads, words) for b in item_bodies(engine, file, at, item)],
    )
    if !runs_in(engine, file, at) { return own }
    let read = entry_read(engine, file)
    let signed? = entry_signed(read) else { return own }
    let entry = kept_body(body_checked(engine, file, signed, false))
    own.concat(metas_read(engine, file, read.store, [r for r in entry.reads if item_holding(read, r.at) == at], words))
}

/// Each of `reads`, standing in `store`, that is a bare name naming a fn among `words` that
/// `@std/meta` declares: where it's read.
fn metas_read(
    engine: QueryEngine,
    file: SourceFileAddress,
    store: SyntaxArena,
    reads: List<NameRead>,
    words: List<string>,
) -> List<Found> {
    [Found { at: store.expr_span(ExprId { index: r.at }), args: [] } for r in reads if r.binder == null && r.home == null && words.contains(r.name) && store.ident_name(ExprId { index: r.at }) != null && names_meta(engine, file, r.name)]
}

/// Whether `name`, read from `file`, names a fn `@std/meta` declares.
fn names_meta(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, name: string) -> bool {
    let d? = resolved(engine, file, Space.Value, name).named() else { return false }
    d.kind == ItemKind.Fn && d.file.package_name == CALLED_META
}

fn embeds_valued(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<Found> {
    meta_values(engine, file, at, ["embed", "provided"])
}

fn guards_valued(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<Found> {
    meta_values(engine, file, at, ["guarded"])
}

/// an embedding fn is called where its path is written, never read as a value
export law embed_is_no_value {
    kind: "type.embed_literal"
    reads: embeds_valued
    voice: embed_words
    witness: "use @std.meta.{embed}\nfn through(f: fn(string) -> string) -> string { f(\"a.txt\") }\nfn read() -> string { through(embed) }\n"
}

/// `guarded` is called where its body is written, never read as a value
export law guard_is_no_value {
    kind: "type.guard_value"
    reads: guards_valued

}

fn embed_words(_a: List<string>) -> Voice { embed_uncalled() }

fn guard_words(_a: List<string>) -> Voice { guard_uncalled() }

}

/// A rewrite's template copied into `store`, holes filled and the names it binds marked `fresh`; absent
/// when it is no template, or can't be read here.
fn copied_template(lang: Language, store: SyntaxArena, said: Rewrite, fresh: string) -> TemplateCopy? {
    let refused: Cell<List<string>> = Cell.new([])
    let sp = Splice {
        lang: lang,
        store: store,
        refused: refused,
        unplaced: list_cell(),
        spliced: map_cell(),
        binders: list_cell(),
        written: nothing_written(),
        of: SpliceOf.Meaning,
        fresh: fresh,
    }
    match said.node {
        .Template(file, at, parts, fills) -> sp.copied(file, at, parts, fills, HoleKind.Statement),
        .Name(_) or .Text(_) or .Int(_) or .Float(_) or .Bool(_) or .Interp(_, _) or .Many(_) -> null,
    }
}

fn net_report(path: string, judge: NetJudge) -> string? {
    let at = if is_a_dir(path) { path } else { dir_of(rooted(path)) }

    let refused: Cell<List<string>> = Cell.new([])
    let sp = Splice {
        lang: avra(),

        refused: refused,
        unplaced: list_cell(),
        spliced: map_cell(),
        binders: list_cell(),
        written: written,
        of: SpliceOf.Generator,

    lambdas_apart(sp.store)
    binders_apart(sp.store, sp.spliced.get(), sp.binders.get(), here)
    SplicedDecls {
        store: sp.store,
        stmts: stmts,
        refused: sp.refused.get(),
        unplaced: sp.unplaced.get(),
    }
}

/// The written item of `file` holding the quote at the offset `at` of its text, none where none
/// does: the item whose text holds the offset, where a quote stands there in it.
@query
fn quote_item(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<int> {
    [i for i in item_ids(engine, file) for start in [item_start(engine, file, i)] if start <= at &&
        at < start + item_under(engine, file, i).text.length &&
        read_item(engine, file, i).store.quote_at(at - start) != null]
        .take(1)
}

/// Every item of `file` by id: its written items, then its generated ones, each in order.
export fn every_item_id(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress) -> List<int> {
    item_ids(engine, file)
        .concat([generated_id(k) for k in 0..file_generated(engine, file).items.length])
}

/// The items of `file` that stand before the item `at`, by id, in order: for a written item, the
/// written ones before it; for a generated one, every written item and the generated ones made
/// before it; every written item where the file holds no `at`.
export fn items_before(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<int> {
    let ids = item_ids(engine, file)
    let k? = generated_rank(at) else {
        let rank = ids.index_of(at)
        return if rank < 0 { ids } else { ids.take(rank) }
    }
    ids.concat([generated_id(j) for j in 0..k])
}

/// Where the item `at` stands among every item of `file`, counted from the first: a written item by
/// its place among the written ones, a generated one past them all by its place among those made;
/// past every written item for one the file doesn't hold. Read without what generators make.
export fn item_order(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> int {
    let ids = item_ids(engine, file)
    let k? = generated_rank(at) else {
        let rank = ids.index_of(at)
        return if rank < 0 { ids.length } else { rank }
    }
    ids.length + k
}

fn made_block(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, site: GeneratorSite, tape: SyntaxTape) -> string {
    let store = new_node_store(spelled_file(file))
    let stmts = item_read_back(store, PlacedTape { start: 0, tape: tape })
    let source = joined([render_statement(store, s) for s in stmts if !store.is_hoisted(s)], "\n\n")
    let template = stmts.find_map((s) -> template_said(engine, store, s)) ?? ""
    "// from @${asked_by(site)} on ${site.name}${template}\n${source}"
}

/// The annotation a site's generator answers to: `derive` for a trait's own, else the fn's name.
fn asked_by(site: GeneratorSite) -> string {
    match site.generator.kind { .Derive -> "derive", rest -> site.generator.name }
}

/// The template a made statement was copied from: its file as the program spells it, and its line
/// there; absent for a statement no template wrote, or one whose file this program doesn't read.
fn template_said(engine: QueryEngine, store: SyntaxArena, s: StmtId) -> string? {
    let origin? = store.stmt_origins.at(s.index) else { return null }
    if !origin.spanned_home { return null }
    let home? = template_file(origin.path) else { return null }
    let text? = source_text(engine, home) else { return null }
    let lo? = store.stmt_span(s)?.lo else { return null }
    if lo > text.length { return null }
    " — template ${spelled_file(home)}:${new_source_file(spelled_file(home), text).linecol(lo).line}"
}

export fn file_problems(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress) -> List<KeptProblem> { file_generated(engine, file).problems.concat(file_validated(engine, file).problems) }

/// What the generators the fn `file` writes as `name` wears make: what the written declaration
/// names, never what generated items do.
export fn fn_generated(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, name: string) -> GeneratedItems {
    let d? = file_declares_named(engine, file, name)
        .names
        .find(it.name == name && it.kind == ItemKind.Fn) else { return said_only([]) }
    gathered_items(
        [site_generated(engine, file, site) for site in declaration_sites(engine, file, d) if !validates(engine, site.generator)],

/// The ids of items keyed `keys`, in order: each its key's and the count of earlier items of that key
/// (`item_id_of`), and where two of those meet, the later moved on past every id taken.
fn item_ids_of(keys: List<string>) -> List<int> {
    mut met: Map<string, int> = {}
    mut taken: Map<string, bool> = {}
    mut ids: List<int> = []
    for key in keys {
        let nth = met.get(key) ?? 0
        met.set(key, nth + 1)
        mut id = item_id_of(key, nth)
        while taken.has("${id}") { id = (id + 1) % GENERATED_FIRST }
        taken.set("${id}", true)
        ids.push(id)
    }
    ids
}

fn binds(store: SyntaxArena, p: PatId) -> bool {
    match store.pat(p) {
        .Bind(_) -> true,
        .Wild or .Rest or .Variant(_, _) or .Member(_, _) or .Lit(_) or .Format(_, _) or .Quote(_) or .Typed(_, _) or .Seq(_, _, _) or .Fields(_, _, _) -> false,

# what one run of the case `$1` said, its warnings aside, its copy's path said as `<case>`: a blank
# line is said only before what is kept, so a warning goes with the line that parts it from the rest
said() {
    sed "s#$tmp/$1#<case>#g" "$tmp/$1.$2" |
        awk '/^warning\[/ { warned = 1; next }

) -> Found {

            "annotation.unplaceable",
            fill_unplaced(p.message),
        )

    if p.unread_home { return carried(null, TEMPLATE_UNREAD, template_unread(p.message)) }
    if p.trapped {

            "annotation.unsettled",
            could_not_run(p.message),
        )

    if p.by == DELEGATING {

            pointed,

        )

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Paths.** The program layer is the default; `AVRA_PROGRAM=0` selects the old path. `AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0` runs the layer alone. The net yields `NetSaid` (Off, Accepted, Refused, Unjudged); `net_stops` steps aside when the program uses forms only the layer builds.
   - **Ids.** `every_item_id` gives written ids, then `generated_id(k) = GENERATED_FIRST (2^40) + k`. `generated_rank(at)` is positional: 8 call sites, in item_generated, law_findings and item_methods. Written ids are keyed: `item_id_of(key, nth)` and `item_ids_of`.
   - **Sites.** `annotated_sites` covers written declarations only (by design: "a site never asks what generators make"). `declared_sites` can read a non-held (generated) item via `read_item`.
   - **Generated item shape.** `GeneratedItems { items, said, problems }`; `KeptProblem` carries the flags unread_home, unrun, trapped and unplaced. `file_generated` is a @cut_query. `site_generated` → `generated` @query, keyed by declaration meaning.
   - **Hygiene.** `lets_kept_apart` renames a hole-bound binder to `apart_name(n) = "${n}$template"`.
   - **Witness cases.** `tools/program-refusals/<case>`: `PIN=1 sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra-try <casename>` (the case NAME, not its path) writes refuses.expected from the old path. The script compares the old `check` against `AVRA_PROGRAM=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 avra build`.
   - **Law witnesses.** The witness manifest is fixed with no dependencies, so a provider must live in the same package, given through `witness_files`.
   - **Lowering walk.** A body with no facts becomes `Missed` with refused 0, so it doesn't refuse. `program_refused` concatenates erring, own, bodies, missed, laws and strays.
   - **Defects.** `defect_at(loc, message)` makes a Diag of kind `language.defect` (diagnostics/mod.av).
   - **Rendering.** `render_among(d, sources)`; `located_files(d)`.
   - **Memory.** Concurrent avra runs contend for the memory pool (AVRA_MEM_POOL), and a run starved of it exits 2. Base and worktree both take about 9.7 GB on quote_mechanical_test.

export type FileWarned = { file: SourceFileAddress, findings: List<LawFinding> }

/// What every law that warns finds in the written items of `file`, each site of one kind once.
@query
export fn file_warned(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress) -> FileWarned {
    let found = [f for at in item_ids(engine, file) for f in findings_in_file(engine, file, at) if !fails_build(f)]
    FileWarned {
        file: file,
        findings: [f for i, f in found if !found.take(i).any((g) -> same_site(g, f))],
    }
}

/// Whether two findings stand at one site under one kind.

/// The quote the file `home` names holds at the offset `at` of its text, as the written item holding
/// it reads back: the store holding it and the quote; absent where none does.
fn written_quote(engine: QueryEngine, home: string, at: int) -> Scratch? {
    let file? = template_file(home) else { return null }
    let i? = quote_item(engine, file, at).first() else { return null }
    let store = read_item(engine, file, i).store
    let q? = store.quote_at(at - item_start(engine, file, i)) else { return null }
    Scratch { store: store, body: q, start: item_start(engine, file, i) }
}

/// The written item of `file` holding the quote at the offset `at` of its text, none where none

fn quote_item(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<int> {
    [i for i in item_ids(engine, file) for start in [item_start(engine, file, i)] if start <= at &&
        at < start + item_under(engine, file, i).text.length &&
        read_item(engine, file, i).store.quote_at(at - start) != null]
        .take(1)
}

### 2026-11-19T22:24:15 LEAD/USER
Lead ruling, the line between the two: a finding inside generated code belongs to whoever WROTE the code it sits in. It's the same law as the dependency-warnings scope defects just landed (a check reports what the checked package wrote). So:
- template code from ANOTHER package, holding none of the checked package's writing: that package's own check judges it, and yours skips it. This is laws-fusion's cut, at the package line, not the file line.
- template code from the SAME package (your generated_fn_body_judged, with the template in a sibling file): judged, homed at the template, because the package wrote it.
- a generated item mixing the user's splices with a dependency's template: judged, with findings kept only at nodes the checked package wrote.
This keeps your witness green and buys back most of the +23%. Measure as you planned.

export type Param = { name: Scoped, ty: TypeRef?, default: ExprId?, promises: SeatMark, @local id: ParamId, marks: List<Mark> = [], state: bool = false, says: List<Param>? = null, prop: bool = false, spread: SeatSpread? = null, implicit: bool = false }

/// What a seat standing for MANY says it is: the call's remaining arguments
/// (`..rest: List<T>`), or a template hole that fills with whole entries
/// (`..${xs}`), the hole's index.
@derive(Identity)
@derive(Taped)
export enum SeatSpread {
    Rest
    Hole(index: int)
}

impl Param {
    /// Whether a call fills it: the receiver's word written bare among a fn's seats, which the naming
    /// law refuses, is no seat.
    fn seated() -> bool { !(self.name.of == RECEIVER && self.ty == null) }

    /// Whether the seat takes the arguments a call leaves.
    fn is_rest() -> bool {
        let held? = self.spread else { return false }
        held is .Rest
    }

    /// The template hole the seat stands for, when it is a hole spread.
    fn spread_hole() -> int? {
        let held? = self.spread else { return null }
        match held { .Hole(index) -> index, .Rest -> null }
    }
}

  - **Unknown result:** `Checking.check` returns `SignedType?`, and `null` means unknown. Seat checks bail on null, or on `.unknown()` (`TypeHead.Unnamed`) or `.inferred()` (checking.av:1033-1037, signed_types.av:421).
  - **`Expr.Error`:** it has no `Checks` impl, so `unruled` and `children_checked` return null (checking.av:1346-1355). It never refuses and absorbs. It is the obvious opaque expression filler.
  - **Unbound name:** `Ident` with no binding records `Unread` via `unbound_read` (checking.av:4072) and returns null. That record later becomes a `resolve` refusal through `unread_placed` (item_refused.av:388) and `unread_in` (item_unresolved.av:31).
  - **Placeholder names are not filtered.** A kept `${k}` name or type would be refused unless `hole_name(name) != null` is filtered in `unread_in` and in the item_unknown_types rows.
  
  ## 5. How generated items are judged
  - **Ids:** `generated_id(k) = GENERATED_FIRST + k` (item_context.av:116-123). `every_item_id` lists the written ids, then the generated ones (item_generated.av:228). `generated_at` indexes `file_generated(...).items` (:575).
  - **Reading:** `item_read` (item_signatures.av:614-626) reads a generated tape back with start 0, held by `made_key`.
  - **`law_findings`** (law_findings.av:98-128): `view` exists only when `item_held`, which is true for written items only. So **node-kind laws never run on generated items**. Only laws that read the item whole run there, e.g. `item_refusals`, which accepts generated items via `item_stands`, item_refused.av:241-268.
  - **`findings_in_file`** sends generated ids to `made_finding` (:256-265). There, `writer_at`/`homed` maps an origin whose path equals `template_home(file)` to the program's own file ("") and keeps the finding. Its spans are already file offsets because of `moved_on`.
  - **Diagnostics:** `file_law_diags` (item_said.av:31) emits them in the provider's file.
  
  ## Cheapest route
  1. Export a door in sugars.av, e.g. `quote_opened(scratch, origin)`. It wraps `template_copied` with fills chosen by kind:
     - Expression and Tail: `Filled.Expr(dst.alloc_expr(Expr.Error))`;
     - Name and Binder: `Filled.Name(placeholder([" "," "],[k]))`, i.e. the hole's own name;
     - Type: `Filled.Type(named_ref("${k}"))`;
     - Inits: `spoiled_inits()`;
     - Statement: `[]`.
     - Origin: `ForeignOrigin{path: template_home(file), spanned_home: true}`.
  2. Add a new query, say `file_quoted(engine, file)`. For each written item and each quote expression in it that is not inside another quote, build the `Scratch`, copy it, and wrap it by `quote_kind`:
     - Decls: the copied statements as they are;
     - Expr/Stmts: a synthetic `fn quote$N() -> _ { … }`;
     - Arms: a `match` over an `Expr.Error` subject.
     - Store `tape_of_item` under a **separate id range**, say `QUOTED_FIRST`, and teach `every_item_id`, `item_stands`, `item_read` and `made_finding` about it.
  3. Filter hole names in the unread-name and unknown-type rows.
  
  ## What would make this hard
  - **Declarations leaking:** putting the item into `file_generated` would add its names to `generated_declares`, the provider's namespace. It would also shift `item_order`/`items_before`, and `site_refused` assumes a site.
  - **Names declared inside the template:** if `fn a() { b() }` and `fn b()` are both in the template, `b` is in no namespace. That needs a scope local to the item, or the template's own names filtered.
  - **Empty fills cause false refusals:** an empty Run gives arity errors, empty Fields or Statement fills give "missing field/method" in `impl Trait`, empty Arms give non-exhaustive matches, and `impl ${t}` has an `Unnamed` target. You need fills shaped like the seat, or to drop findings at nodes a hole holds.
  - **Templates whose holes hold nodes:** sugar `Rewrite` templates hold node fills and are written in `@std.meta` modules. Decide whether to include them.
  - **Nested quotes** are copied verbatim, so skip a quote inside a synthetic item to avoid recursion.
  - **Cost:** this is one extra item per quote in every file.

### 2026-11-19T22:31:45 AGENT
While those finish, here's the design for (A), so the lead can correct it before I build it:

1. **Quoted items in the provider.** A new per-file query makes one synthetic item per top-level quote in the file's written items. Each is the quote's body copied through the existing `template_copied` path, with opaque fills chosen by hole kind: `Expr.Error` for an expression (it absorbs and never refuses), the hole's own name for a name or binder, and so on. They get their own id range, not `file_generated`, so a template's `fn gone` never becomes a declaration of the provider's file. Every law judges them, and findings are homed at the quote in the provider's file.
2. **"Judged for what it can say".** A finding at a node a hole holds, or one that reads a hole name, is dropped there. That part stays the instance's.
3. **Downstream.** A generated item whose writers are all another package's templates is skipped whole. In a mixed item, findings are kept only at the checked package's own nodes. Same-package templates are judged as now.

/// A declaration-GENERATING annotation reaches only literals: its
/// generated names must exist before the file's names are known, so
/// its arguments run at the same moment, before any typed answer.
fn computed_argument(mut cx: TypeCx, a: Annotation) {

        .spoken(
            refusal(
                "annotation.seats",
                at_annotation(cx, a),

/// A quote's holes classified — the kind of each, by its index.
export fn hole_kinds(store: SyntaxArena, e: ExprId) -> List<HoleKind> {
    let bp? = store.expr(e).body_of() else { return [] }
    match bp.view {
        .Verbatim(ss, arms) -> {

            let _ = rb.stmts(ss)

            rb.kinds

        .None -> [HoleKind.Expression for h in bp.holes],
        .Expanded(_) -> [],
    }
}

/// What a quote's body PARSED as.
export fn quote_kind(store: SyntaxArena, e: ExprId) -> QuoteKind {
    let bp? = store.expr(e).body_of() else { return QuoteKind.Stmts }
    match bp.view {
        .Verbatim(ss, arms) -> {
            if !arms.is_empty() { return QuoteKind.Arms }
            if ss.is_empty() { return QuoteKind.Stmts }
            if ss.all((s: StmtId) -> store.bare_hole(s)) { return QuoteKind.Holes }
            if store.hole_stmt(ss.last()!) == null && store.answer_of(ss.last()!) != null {
                return QuoteKind.Expr
            }
            if ss.all((s: StmtId) -> store.declares(s) || store.hole_stmt(s) != null) { return QuoteKind.Decls }
            QuoteKind.Stmts
        },
        .None or .Expanded(_) -> QuoteKind.Stmts,
    }
}

- **Unparsed template:** a template whose file didn't parse is not copied. `build` and `check` now say the same single parse refusal, and `template_unparsed_said_once` is red on base, green after.
- **Defect voice:** lowering's catch-all now speaks as `language.defect`, so a body reaching lowering unjudged is loud.
- **Homing by writer:** a finding in generated code goes to whoever wrote the node it stands on. This fixed `refuses_in_wrapped_body`, which had been homed in the wrong file, and both idioms reds.
- **Refused declarations:** a generated item over a declaration a law already refuses isn't judged. This fixed the three formats reds, where a duplicated `grammar` cascaded into its door.

**(A) is written in a new worktree (/work/avra-i4) but not built or tried yet:**
- **Provider side:** each template a package writes is opened in its own file with placeholder fills and judged by every law, as a quoted item outside the file's declarations. A finding standing on a hole, or holding one, is dropped, because the fill decides it.
- **Downstream:** a generated item that holds none of the checked package's writing isn't judged at all, which is laws-fusion's cost cut at the package line. Findings at nodes another package wrote are dropped.
- **New spec file:** `template_judged_test.av` has four cases. Three check the provider itself and one checks that a dependent hears the template's error once.
- **Open scope:** only declaring quotes are opened for now. Expression and statement quotes aren't judged yet.

The new spec file carries red/green there instead. I expect the existing witnesses to keep holding, now said once from the provider's quote.
- Quote tests that expect a template's error at the instance may need moving to the provider's check, as you ruled.

s = s[:m.start()] + rep + s[m.end():]

The base57 merge is resolved and committed as c2c08857, but it doesn't build, so I haven't bundled `base57..HEAD`. I've posted this to the lead as a blocker.

`@derive(Saved)` on `Seating` runs out of its 5 MiB compile-time budget. base57 alone fits. My branch adds one variant, `.Capacity`, which says that a `produce` or `channel` capacity isn't an `int`. That came from my earlier lane, which didn't ride batch 57, and that one variant tips the derive over. I confirmed it with three different builders, the last being base57's own freshly built compiler: base57 builds, the merge doesn't, and std-program and std-meta are identical between them.

Separately, base57's committed bootstrap seed refuses base57's own std-text, so building from that seed fails even on base57 itself.

I gave the lead three options:
- **Raise std-avrac's budget** in its manifest under `[lifted]`, re-measured. The design allows this, but it's a manifest decision.
- **Lighten the `Saved` derive** for large enums. That code is std-program's, shared, not mine.
- **Drop `.Capacity`.** I don't recommend it: no existing variant fits, so the refusal would name the wrong thing.

Meanwhile, ruling (A) continues in i4, which builds from 3e377552 without base57. It's rebuilt with the latest rule (a name a hole lands is the instance's). A sweep is running with each compiler checking its own tree:
- the five template witnesses;
- the layer's `check` of std-avrac, std-program, cli, std-meta and std-relation, compared i3 against i4;
- the quote and annotations feature suites.

program layer: a template is judged where it is written, once, in the package that wrote it

Ruling (A). A refusal inside a template is its author's. It is said in the check of the package
that writes the quote, at the quote, once. It is never said again in each program that splices it.

- Quoted items (file_quoted, ids from QUOTED_FIRST). Each declaring quote of a file's written items
  is opened where it is written. It is copied through the splice door with every hole filled by a
  placeholder of its own (`$holeN`), which no program can write. It becomes an item no file
  declares and nothing runs, judged by every law. Its fns are typed through its own item. Its
  impls are typed even where a hole names the target, with a receiver of no type it can know.
- What a fill decides stays the instance's:
  - a finding on a hole, or one holding a hole (a name's resolution only on one);
  - one where the quote opens, where a fill with no place of its own lands;
  - one reading a placeholder;
  - whether a fn may read `self` (where it lands decides if it is a method);
  - a name a hole that lands seats or statements may bind.
  A template's reads of the names it declares stand. A binder a hole names never reads by its
  written name, so that read is still the template's.
- Downstream (the ruling's cut, at the package line). A generated item holding none of the checked
  package's writing is not judged here: it is the template's package's to judge. In any generated
  item, a finding at a node another package's template wrote is dropped. A lowering refusal in such
  an item is its template's, said where the template is written (refused_where_written), not a
  defect. file_erring counts what the file's diagnostics say, so the two never disagree.

- features/quote/tests/template_judged_test.av (4/4, red before): the provider's own check refuses

### 2026-11-20T04:01:50 AGENT
The extra cost was my own regression, and it's fixed in i4 but not yet committed or measured cleanly.

On every splice, `home_unparsed` (added in 3e377552) re-read every item of the template's file, looking for a parse refusal, with nothing cached. That made the `generated` query 60% slower, which accounted for nearly all of item 2's +11%. It's now one cached answer per file, in the same pattern as `strays_in`.

A single cold profiled build afterwards shows total query time at +2.3% over the compiler from before item 2. What's left is the real work: about 1.2 s judging generated and quoted bodies, and 1.1 s more in generation. A two-round cold measurement of `check` and `build` is running now to confirm against the +2% budget. Commit, receipts and the bundle follow.

### 2026-11-20T05:53:47 AGENT
The six `decl_grain_test` reds are still there; it's a different cause than I first fixed.

That test edits `lib`, then checks the caller recomputes no more queries than a bystander that doesn't reach `lib`. The caller's build asks `file_quoted(lib)` (whether lib's templates refuse), but the bystander only asks for lib's warnings, which never ask it. So the caller recomputes one query name the bystander doesn't. `lib` writes no template at all, so asking was wasted work anyway.

The fix: only a file whose text contains `quote` is asked for its quoted items. Every other file asks nothing beyond its items, which both sides already ask. i4 is rebuilding to rerun `decl_grain_test` and the template spec.

Idioms are clean now, and `template_judged_test` (4/4) and `quote_test` (16/16) held on the last build. If both pass, I'll commit and rerun the full receipts.

## Where it was first seen

A private `type Held` added to std-relation's `relation.av` broke every in-package test of
std-relation. `src/tests/frame_law_test.av` declares its own `type Held = { @key name:
string, n: int }`, and the `@relation` derive's record literals bound to the provider's
`Held`. The errors were "`Held` has no field `name`" and "the body answers `Held` but
`insert` declares `Held`". The workaround was to rename the private type to `CodecHolds`,
in `b6a51c14f` on the since-deleted `svc/codec-cost` branch.

/// What the law `l`, which judges no kind of node, finds in the item `at` of `file` read whole: from
/// the file, and through `view` where the file holds the item.
fn read_whole(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int, view: ItemView?, l: LawEntry) -> List<
    Found,
> {
    let read = (l.reads)(engine, file, at)
    let v? = view else { return read }
    let seen = (l.reads_view)(v)
    if seen.is_empty() { return read }
    if read.is_empty() { seen } else { read.concat(seen) }
}

/// Whether the finding `a` stands before `b` in its file: a placed one before an unplaced one.
fn stands_before(a: LawFinding, b: LawFinding) -> bool {
    let there? = b.at else { return a.at != null }
    let here? = a.at else { return false }
    here.lo < there.lo
}

/// A provider whose `Again` makes a record wearing `@derive(Twice)`, and whose `Twice` gives a
/// record a method; and `Forever`, whose record wears `@derive(Forever)` again.
fn rounds_provider() -> string {
    "use @std.meta.{Type, Directive, beside, derive}\n" +
        "export trait Twice {\n" +
        "    static fn derive(t: Type) -> List<Directive> {\n" +

        "export trait Again {\n" +
        "    static fn derive(t: Type) -> List<Directive> {\n" +

        "}\n" +
        "export trait Forever {\n" +
        "    static fn derive(t: Type) -> List<Directive> {\n" +
        "        [beside(t, quote {\n            @derive(Forever)\n            type \${t}_x = { x: int }\n        })]\n" +
        "    }\n" +
        "}\n"
}

Rounds are written in i5 but not yet built or tested, because a build now would compete with the gates for memory:
- **Generated ids carry their round:** a generated item's id is `GENERATED_FIRST + round × 2^32 + a key`. The key comes from the item's meaning, as warm's scheme does for written items, so an edit that leaves an item's meaning alone leaves its id alone.
- **Each round reads only the rounds before it.** `round_generated(file, r)` makes round r from per-item `made_sites` queries over round r−1's items. That avoids the cycle that blocked this before. `file_generated` gathers the rounds, up to 8.
- **Depth bound:** beyond 8 rounds it says "generation runs deeper than 8 rounds" and names the chain of generators (`annotation.generation_depth`), with a witness and code row.
- **Problems on generated declarations are now said.** A generator's problem with a generated declaration used to be dropped silently, which is exactly why `derive_default_silent` printed nothing.

fn trait_place(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, item: ReadItem, name: string) -> Loc? {
    let s? = item.stmts.find((x: StmtId) -> item.store.trait_parts(x)?.name == name) else { return null }
    meta_place(engine, file, item, item.store.stmt_span(s))
}

/// A span of `file` as the place a meta value names: its file spelled by package and path.
fn meta_place(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, item: ReadItem, span: Span?) -> Loc? {
    let held? = span else { return null }
    let own? = item.at else { return counted_in_item(engine, file, held) }
    Loc { file: item_spelled(file, own), lo: held.lo, hi: held.hi }
}

/// A place `file` counts from its start, as a crossed place counts it: from the start of the item
/// that holds it, and spelled with that item; absent where no item holds it.
fn counted_in_item(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, span: Span) -> Loc? {
    let p? = placed_in_item(engine, file, FindingAt { lo: span.lo, hi: span.hi }) else { return null }
    Loc { file: item_spelled(file, p.item), lo: p.at.lo, hi: p.at.hi }
}

The nullable comparison is reproduced and has a fix written in i5. It isn't built or tested yet, because the bisect builds are using the memory pool.
- **Reproduction:** with `type Scoped = Name` and `Name` a one-field record, `a == b` for `a: Scoped?`, `b: Scoped` is accepted by the old path. The layer refuses it: "`==` compares matching types, found `Scoped?` and `Scoped`".
- **Fix:** the layer's equality check compares each side by its underlying shape, and that lookup doesn't see through a nullable named type. A nullable side now takes its shape from its non-null form, made nullable again, so `Scoped?` against `Scoped` compares as `Name?` against `Name`, which is already accepted. The change is confined to comparisons.

Named: the edit-a `derived` failure is mine, from c4aa476f (in the base57..69e7ae21 bundle).
- `home_read` (a template naming a file the program doesn't read) asked `package_sources` on every splice. That reads the directory listing, which moves with every file written beside it, so editing one record reran every generator.
- Fix: `home_read` becomes a @cut_query. It recomputes as the listing moves, but its answer stands, so no splice reruns. On the `derived` probe, only the edited record's generator runs again.

The edit-witness regression has a cause and a fix.

My own commit c4aa476f, already in the batch-58 bundle, made every generator run check whether its template's file is part of the program by reading the package's directory listing. That listing changes whenever any file in the directory is written, so editing one record reran every generator in the file. That check is now cached once per template file. It's recomputed when the listing changes, but its answer stays the same, so nothing rebuilt from it reruns. In the reproduction, editing one of three records now reruns only that record's generator.

The fix is committed on the lane branch. It's rebuilding with the net off and running every edit-witness row, edit-a through edit-g, which my earlier receipts never covered. I'll send a corrected bundle once they pass, and I've told the lead to keep holding the last bundle's edit-a row until then.

fn pointed_written(engine: QueryEngine, store: SyntaxArena, p: KeptProblem) -> Span? {

generation in rounds: a generated declaration's generators run over it, in the next round

written one's do. This fixes derive_default_silent: a component `@formed` emits is now composed, and
its `@attr` mark is refused (`@std/ui:marked-composition`), as the old path says it.

- Rounds. `round_generated(file, r)`: round 0 is what the written declarations' generators make;
  round r is what the generators named by each round r-1 item's declarations make. `file_generated`
  gathers them, up to `GENERATION_ROUNDS` (8).
- Ids carry their round. `GENERATED_FIRST + round·2^32 + key`, the key from the item's meaning and
  nth, as written items' ids are keyed (`round_ids_of`). `generated_rank` is gone: every positional
  use reads ids (`generated_ids`, `is_generated`, `generated_round`), and a generated item's impls
  are read off its own tape.
- Per item, so a warm edit reruns only the rounds its item feeds (condition 1):
  - `made_sites(file, at)` is a query per generated item.
  - `made_item(file, at)` and `made_declared_named(file, name)` are cut queries, so a round's item
    read by id or by name stands while its neighbours move.
  - A round reads only the rounds before it, so there is no cycle.
- Witness, edit-a's new part `rounds`: three records each `@derive(Again)`, each making a record
  `@derive(Count)`. The middle one given a field reruns its chain alone, two generator runs, once a
  round; warm == cold, and back.
- The depth bound (condition 2): a chain past 8 rounds is refused once, at the written annotation
  that began it, naming the chain. The voice is `annotation.generation_depth`: "generation runs
  deeper than 8 rounds: @derive(Forever) → …". Its witness and code row are in place, golden
  rounds_test.av.
- A copied annotation names its generator where its template was written (`written_home`).
- A generated declaration's places are its template's:
  - `meta_place` counts a span of a generated item in the file whose template wrote it;
  - marks' and annotations' spans move with their nodes when a written template is copied
    (`Rebuilder.moved_by`);
  - a problem with a generated declaration points in its template's file (`pointed_written`).
- A generator's problem with a generated declaration is said: the problems law reads generated items
  too (`made_problems_said`).
- A derive's problem is said as refused by its trait (`derive_said`), as the old path says it: a
  written component's `@attr` composition now reads "refused by `View`" on the layer too.

The old path is unchanged (condition 3).

#!/bin/sh
# THE avra COMMAND — the compiler, hosted by itself. `build/avra` is
# the working binary; it rebuilds from `make avra`, which uses the
# binary that is already there. The seed is the cold path, and it is
# taken only when there is no binary at all.
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
# THE CALLER'S DIRECTORY, kept before this script moves to the tree's
# root: a command that reads "the package I stand in" (`explain`)
# roots there, never at the tree — `cd` below rewrites PWD too.
AVRA_CWD="$(pwd)"
export AVRA_CWD
# the link flags a manifest writes as ${LLVM_PREFIX}
LLVM_PREFIX="${LLVM_PREFIX:-/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm}"
export LLVM_PREFIX
# the static LLVM link's platform answers (packages/std-avrac/avra.toml)
if [ "$(uname -s)" = Darwin ]; then
    AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME="${AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME:-c++}"
    AVRA_SYS_SEARCH="${AVRA_SYS_SEARCH:-/opt/homebrew/lib}"
    export AVRA_SYS_SEARCH
else

// The totality invariant, live: every expression has a TypeId —
// holes and unresolved names type as Error — and Error absorbs
// without cascading a second diagnostic. Everything reaches the
// pass through the driver's one artifact.
use @std.avrac.compiler.{analyze_source, Analysis}
use core.{Type, TypeId}

// Plain-fn shape tests: a method call in a lambda body would bind
// `it` at ITS fold (innermost method wins); a plain call leaves the
// pronoun to the scan that owns it.
fn int_shape(a: Analysis, id: TypeId) -> bool { a.view.decls.types.shape_of(id) is .Int }
fn err_shape(a: Analysis, id: TypeId) -> bool { a.view.decls.types.shape_of(id) is .Error }

/// Error-typed slots in one analysis.
fn holes(a: Analysis) -> int {
    a.facts.of_expr.ids(err_shape(a, it)).length
}

// Typing, as a program says it: an unresolved name or a hole speaks once and never cascades into a
// second diagnostic, every body of a file is typed, and what several bodies say reads in source order.
use @std.avrac.testing.{judged}

spec "compiler/typing" {
    given "a clean program" {
        then "every expression types, idents through their definition, and nothing is said" {
            judged("let x = 1 + 2\nx").diagnostics.is_empty()
        }
    }
    given "an unresolved name in an expression" {
        then "it is said once, and typing adds no echo" {
            judged("let x = 1 + y").diagnostics.length == 1
        }
    }
    given "a recovery hole between good statements" {
        then "the hole is said once, and the statements around it type silently" {
            judged("let a = 1\nlet = 3\nlet y = 2").diagnostics.length == 1
        }
    }
    given "several declarations in one file" {
        then "every body types — the file checks clean" {
            judged(
                "type P = { x: int }\nenum E {\n    a\n    b\n}\nfn f(p: P) -> int {\n    p.x\n}\nfn g(e: E) -> int {\n    match e {\n        .a -> 1\n        .b -> 2\n    }\n}\nf(P { x: 1 }) + g(E.b)",
            )
                .diagnostics
                .is_empty()
        }
        then "two erroring bodies report in SOURCE order, whatever order they were asked in" {
            // the entry calls `b` before `a`, so `b`'s body is asked first; the report still reads
            // top to bottom.
            let p = judged("fn a() -> int {\n    \"s\"\n}\nfn b() -> int {\n    true\n}\nb() + a()")
            p.diagnostics.length == 2 &&
                p.diagnostics[0].message.contains("`a` declares") &&
                p.diagnostics[1].message.contains("`b` declares")
        }
    }
    given "a use before its definition" {
        then "the use is said once, and typing stays quiet" {
            judged("x\nlet x = 1").diagnostics.length == 1
        }
    }
}

// A top-level `state` is a place a body reads: a fn that reads one, directly or through a callee, is
// never constant — what it answers follows the state as it is when it is called, never as it stood
// when the program was made.
use @std.avrac.testing.{judged, shown}

spec "features/read_set — a top-level state is never constant" {
    given "a fn reading one directly" {
        then "it answers the state as it is at the call" {
            shown("state n: int = 0\nfn f() -> int { n + 1 }\nn = 5\nf()") == "6"
        }
    }
    given "a caller of a fn reading one" {
        then "the caller answers it too, through the callee" {
            shown("state n: int = 0\nfn g() -> int { n }\nfn f() -> int { g() + 1 }\nn = 5\nf()") == "6"
        }
    }
    given "a fn reading no state" {
        then "it answers its own constant whatever the state holds, and the program is clean" {
            let text = "state n: int = 0\nfn f() -> int { 1 + 2 }\nn = 5\nf() + n"
            judged(text).clean() && shown(text) == "8"
        }
    }
}
EOF

/// refuses at build, so a refusal stands where it is said. Empty for a run that answers, and for a
/// refusal no kind heads.
fn run_refusal(r: Result<string, string>) -> string {
    let e? = match r { .Err(e) -> e, .Ok(_) -> null } else { return "" }
    let head = e.split("\n")[0]
    if !head.starts_with("error[") { return "" }
    let close = head.index_of("]: ")
    if close < 0 { return "" }
    "${head.substring(6, close)}: ${head.substring(close + 3, head.length)}"
}

//! A BUILD'S OBJECTS ARE A FUNCTION OF WHAT THEY ARE MADE FOR. Every key a build's objects make
//! holds `objects_salt`: the compiler, the backend's code, the level, the inlining, the target, what
//! the binary links and the tools that link it. So an object made for one target never answers for
//! another, and the same build asked again keys alike.
use commands.{BinaryAsked, salted_by}
use @std.program.{SourceFileAddress}

/// A native dev build of one file, as a build asks for it.
fn asked() -> BinaryAsked {
    BinaryAsked {
        entry: SourceFileAddress { package_name: "app", path_in_package: "src/main.av" },
        compiler: "avra",
        head: [],
        words: [],
        linked: ["runtime"],
        dir: "/w/.avra-cache/tapes-build",
        opt: "-O0",
        layered: true,
        inlined: true,
    }
}

spec "commands/tapes — the salt every object key holds" {
    given "the same build asked twice" {
        then "it salts its objects alike" { salted_by(asked(), "h") == salted_by(asked(), "h") }

            salted_by(asked() with { target: "wasm32-wasip1" }, "h") != salted_by(asked(), "h")

The removal stands, and I've also taken the four off Code's API.
Where they're declared: std-avrac's own `features.Code` (features/code.av, `impl Code`). `@std/meta`'s Code is a separate `{ node: Node }` and has none of them.

/// The present arm: its name bound to what the subject carries, in a scope of its own; an arm that
/// answers what it binds where the match answers the subject's own type is the subject itself.
fn present_arm(mut cx: Lowering, m: MatchOpt, e: ExprId, v: Reg) -> Reg {
    let held = cx.type_at(m.subject)!
    if cx.store.ident_name(m.present) == m.bind.of && cx.type_at(e)?.spelled() == held.spelled() { return v }
    cx.opened()
    cx.bind(m.bind.of, Bound.Value(cx.carried(v, held), held.unwrapped()))
    let r = cx.lower(m.present)
    cx.closed()
    r
}

impl StmtLowers for LetElse {
    /// A region on the subject's presence whose answer is the binding: what the subject carries, or
    /// where it's absent, the `else`, which leaves.
    fn stmt_lowered(mut cx: Lowering, s: StmtId) {
        let held? = cx.type_at(self.subject) else { return cx.stmt_unlowered(s) }
        let v = cx.lower(self.subject)

            .region(cx.present(v, held), cx.laid_out(carried)) { cx -> cx.carried(v, held) } else { cx ->
                cx.opened()
                for st in self.stmts { cx.lower_stmt(st) }
                cx.closed()
                cx.hollow_of(carried)
            }
        cx.bind(self.name.of, Bound.Value(r, carried))
    }
}

//! WHAT A TYPE IS TO THE MACHINE, IN A WORD — `avra repr`'s answer: a type expression read where a
//! file's top level stands, laid out as the program lays it out (`CheckedProgram.layout`), and named
//! by what that layout is. A nullable answers by what carries its absence; anything else by whether
//! it rides a pointer.
use core.{BoxKind, Layout}
use @std.program.address.{SourceFileAddress}
use @std.program.query_engine.{QueryEngine}

/// The representation of the type `text` spells, read in `file`: absent for text that spells no
/// type, a name `file` reads as no type, or a type no value has.
export fn type_repr(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, text: string) -> string? {
    let written? = parse_type_ref(avra(), text) else { return null }
    let signing = signing_in(engine, file, [])
    let ty = signing.signed(written)
    if ty.unknown() { return null }
    let program = program_of(engine, file, signing)
    let whole? = program.layout(ty) else { return null }
    if !ty.nullable() { return carried_word(whole) }
    let carried? = program.layout(ty.unwrapped()) else { return null }
    absence_word(whole, carried)
}

/// A value that is no nullable: whether it rides a pointer.
fn carried_word(l: Layout) -> string { if l.pointer() { "boxed" } else { "flat" } }

/// A nullable laid out as `whole` over a value laid out as `carried`, by what carries its absence:
/// the value's own pointer, null (niche); a box of one slot around a flat record; a presence flag
/// beside the value (pair); or a tag no variant has.
fn absence_word(whole: Layout, carried: Layout) -> string {
    match whole {
        .Maybe(_) -> "pair",
        .Boxed(box) -> match box {
            .Slot -> "one-slot box",
            .Text or .Bytes or .List or .Map or .Record or .Enum or .Closure or .Cell or .Task or .Dyn or .Union or .Range -> "niche",
        },
        .Bare -> "niche",
        .Void or .Word or .Truth or .Real or .Fields(_) or .Tagged(_) -> if carried.pointer() { "niche" } else { "tag -1" },
    }
}

// A record's SLOTS as the runtime lays them out: a flat record of scalars rides inline in a box that
// holds it, one slot per scalar; a record that is not flat takes one slot. Flatness does not nest — a
// record holding a flat record is boxed, though it still lays that flat record inline in its own box.
// So a nested all-scalar record cannot shift a reader's index. Each count is the program layer's
// layout (`CheckedProgram.layout`), as the backend, the evaluator and the memory pass read it.
use @std.avrac.testing.{judged}
use compiler.{signing_in, program_of, parse_type_ref, avra}
use core.{Layout}

const shapes: string = "type Inner = { p: bool, q: bool }\ntype Pair = { x: int, y: int }\ntype Mid = { x: int, inner: Inner }\ntype Outer = { a: int, pair: Pair, mid: Mid, s: string }\ntype Nested = { m: List<Inner>, inner: Inner, t: string }\n0\n"

/// What a value of the type `text` spells is to the machine, in the shapes' program.
fn layout_of(text: string) -> Layout? {
    let j = judged(shapes)
    let signing = signing_in(j.engine, j.entry, [])
    let written? = parse_type_ref(avra(), text) else { return null }
    program_of(j.engine, j.entry, signing).layout(signing.signed(written))
}

/// The slots each field of a record takes in the box that holds it, in field order.
fn slots_of(fields: List<string>) -> string { ["${layout_of(f)?.slots() ?? 0}" for f in fields].join(",") }

/// Whether the type `text` spells rides inline: a flat record, carried as its fields.
fn flat(text: string) -> bool { layout_of(text) is .Fields }

spec "features/crossing — a record's slots" {
    given "a flat record of scalars" {
        then "is flat, and rides inline in its container, one slot per scalar" {
            flat("Pair") && flat("Inner") && slots_of(["int", "Pair"]) == "1,2"
        }
    }
    given "a record that holds a flat record, inside a container" {
        then "is itself boxed — flatness does not nest — and takes one slot" {
            !flat("Mid") && !flat("Outer") && slots_of(["int", "Pair", "Mid", "string"]) == "1,2,1,1"
        }
    }
    given "a record that holds a flat record and a scalar" {
        then "takes the slots its own fields spell, the flat one inline" {
            slots_of(["int", "Inner"]) == "1,2"
        }
    }
    given "a record beside a list of flat records" {
        then "the list is one slot and a flat field spells its scalars" {
            slots_of(["List<Inner>", "Inner", "string"]) == "1,2,1"
        }
    }
}
EOF

//! A settlement is billed for what ITS OWN run holds. `type_named` asks the
//! workspace, which builds types and signatures to answer and keeps them —
//! memory the compiler made on the run's behalf, never the run's. A budget
//! that counted it made a derive's fate depend on how much the compiler had
//! already loaded: the same derive settled in 2 MB or was cut off past 5 MiB,
//! and the cut dropped its declarations without a word.
use @std.avrac.testing.old_path.{typed_ir_of}
use @std.avrac.core.{Ins, Reg}
use @std.avrac.features.{Unsettled, Lifted, MetaVal, new_meta_heap, budgets_of}
use compiler.backend.{run_crossed}
use compiler.lower.{Body, Lowered}

/// An entry that asks the workspace for `X` before its own answer.
fn asks_the_workspace() -> Lowered {
    let base = typed_ir_of("fn f() -> int { 3 }\nf()")
    let plain: Body = base.fns.first()!
    let e = plain with { name: base.entry.name }
    let at = e.reg_types.length
    let text = Reg { index: at }
    let answer = Reg { index: at + 1 }
    // LICENSED compiler.raw_rt_call: the witness hand-builds the one instruction whose row reaches the workspace
    let kept = e with { ins: [Ins.ConstStr(text, "X"), Ins.CallRt(answer, "avra_type_named", [text])].concat(e.ins), reg_types: e.reg_types.concat([e.reg_types[0], e.reg_types[0]]), layouts: e.layouts.concat([e.layouts[0], e.layouts[0]]) }
    base with { entry: kept, fns: [] }
}

@codec

/// The code of these bodies and statics, and the hashes they ask. Each
/// type is read by its shape, once.
export fn code_facts(decls: Decls, bodies: List<Body>, statics: List<Static>, asked: List<string>) -> CodeFacts {

        }
    }
    read_code_facts(lowered, statics, asked, typed_reading(shapes))
}

//! A TYPE'S SHAPE KEY is a function of the type alone: the same declarations key alike whichever

//! the program layer the key is what a fn's code hash reads of each type it carries
//! (`code_hash(answer)`, code_hash_test's `hash_in`), so a cycle of types declared in any order
//! hashes alike, and a member of the cycle that moves moves it.

/// The cycle A → B → C → A, and D over all three, declared in `order`.
fn cyclic(order: List<string>) -> string {
    let decls: Map<string, string> = {
        "A": "type A = { b: B?, n: int }",
        "B": "type B = { a: A?, c: C?, m: string }",
        "C": "type C = { b: B?, a: A? }",
        "D": "type D = { a: A, c: C, b: B }",
    }
    [decls.get(n)! for n in order].join("\n")
}

/// The cycle declared in `order`, and an `answer` carrying `through`.
fn reaching(order: List<string>, through: string) -> string { "${cyclic(order)}\nfn answer(x: ${through}) -> int { 1 }" }

}

// A file's rule findings are the same whether the file is judged whole or one declaration at a
// time: a rule's subject is one node, so a declaration is the grain a per-item answer takes — and

use @std.avrac.testing.{judged}

/// What `avra check` finds in a one-file program, each as its rule and its line.
fn found(source: string) -> List<string> { ["${f.rule}: ${f.text}" for f in judged(source).findings()] }

/// The findings of a file of `decls` over the entry `entry`, judged whole.
fn whole(decls: List<string>, entry: string) -> string { found(decls.join("\n") + "\n" + entry).join("\n") }

/// The findings of each declaration of `decls` judged alone, each over the same entry, in order.
fn split(decls: List<string>, entry: string) -> string {
    [d + "\n" + entry for d in decls].map((p) -> found(p).join("\n")).filter(it != "").join("\n")
}

spec "compiler/rule_pass (split by declaration)" {
    given "findings in several declarations" {
        then "three dead parameters render alike whole and split" {
            let decls = ["fn a(x: int) -> int { 1 }", "fn b(y: int) -> int { 2 }", "fn c(z: int) -> int { 3 }"]
            let w = whole(decls, "a(0) + b(0) + c(0)")
            w == [found("${d}\n${n}(0)").join("\n") for d in decls for n in [d.substring(3, 4)]].join("\n") &&
                w.split("dead_parameter").length == 4
        }
        then "a licence on the line above a finding stands in both" {
            let decls = ["// LICENSED fns.dead_parameter: kept for the seat\nfn a(x: int) -> int { 1 }", "fn b(y: int) -> int { 2 }"]
            let w = whole(decls, "a(0) + b(0)")
            w == [found("${decls[0]}\na(0)").join("\n"), found("${decls[1]}\nb(0)").join("\n")].filter(it != "").join("\n") &&
                w.split("dead_parameter").length == 2
        }
        then "a clean file has no findings either way" {
            whole(["fn a(x: int) -> int { x }"], "a(1)") == "" && split(["fn a(x: int) -> int { x }"], "a(1)") == ""
        }
    }
}

    file_docs(j.engine, j.entry).decls.find(it.name == name)
}

fn doc_of(source: string, name: string) -> List<string>? { doc_entry(source, name)?.doc }

fn annotations_of(source: string, name: string) -> List<string> { doc_entry(source, name)?.annotations ?? [] }

/// The rule's Code over the top-level statement that declares `name`.
fn declaring(source: string, name: string) -> Code? {
    let items = judged(source).rule_items("/alone/src/main.av")
    [Code { of: i.file, at: At.Stmt(s) } for i in items for s in i.stmts if i.file.view.store.declared_name(s) == name].first()
}

spec "declaration facts — one door, every declaration" {
    given "a fn" {
        then "its `///` lines come back, in written order" {
            (doc_of("/// line one\n/// line two\nfn f() -> int {\n    1\n}\nf()", "f") ?? []).join("\n") == "line one\nline two"
        }
        then "no `///` at all reads null, never an empty-but-present list" {
            doc_of("fn f() -> int {\n    1\n}\nf()", "f") == null
        }
        then "its `@name(args)` come back in written order, with literal argument text" {
            annotations_of("fn tag(s: string, n: int) { }\n@tag(\"x\", 3)\nfn f() -> int {\n    1\n}\nf()", "f") == ["@tag(\"x\", 3)"]
        }
        then "no annotation at all reads an empty list" {
            annotations_of("fn f() -> int {\n    1\n}\nf()", "f").is_empty()
        }
        then "stacked annotations keep the author's order" {
            annotations_of("fn a() { }\nfn b(n: int) { }\n@a\n@b(1)\nfn f() -> int {\n    1\n}\nf()", "f").join(",") == "@a(),@b(1)"
        }
    }
    given "a type" {
        then "its doc and its annotation both read back" {
            let src = "fn tag() { }\n/// a pair\n@tag\ntype P = { x: int, y: int }\nP { x: 1, y: 2 }.x"
            (doc_of(src, "P") ?? []).join("\n") == "a pair" && annotations_of(src, "P") == ["@tag()"]
        }
    }
    given "a const" {
        then "its doc reads back" { (doc_of("/// the answer\nconst K: int = 42\nK", "K") ?? []).join("\n") == "the answer" }
    }
    given "the Code door (features/code.av), which every rule holds" {
        then "annotations() reads the declaring statement's own, as the docs door does" {
            let c? = declaring("fn tag() { }\n/// documented\n@tag\nfn f() -> int {\n    1\n}\nf()", "f") else { return false }
            c.annotations().length == 1 && c.annotations()[0].name == "tag"
        }
        then "a node that is not itself a declaring statement answers empty, not its enclosing fn's" {
            let items = judged("fn tag() { }\n@tag\nfn f() -> int {\n    1\n}\nf()").rule_items("/alone/src/main.av")
            let fns = [Code { of: i.file, at: At.Stmt(s) } for i in items for s in i.stmts if i.file.view.store.declared_name(s) == "f"]
            fns.length == 1 && fns[0].kids().all(it.annotations().is_empty())
        }
    }
    given "a file that opens with a `//!` header" {
        then "a declaration with no `///` of its own reads none — the header is the file's" {
            let src = "//! What this file is for.\nfn f() -> int {\n    1\n}\nf()\n"
            doc_of(src, "f") == null && (file_docs(judged(src).engine, judged(src).entry).header ?? []).join("\n") == "What this file is for."
        }
    }
}

```
// Fixtures shared by the tests that stand a workspace over memory files: one
// process's own workspace with every file admitted, a file checked in it, and the
// family ordinals a test builds a `Key` from.
use @std.avrac.testing.old_path.{test_workspace}
use compiler.{Workspace, rule_findings, analysed}
use compiler.host.{memory_host}
use compiler.families.{Family}
use core.{DeclId}

/// A family's ordinal, found by its name: ordinals move when a family is added or
/// converted, names do not.
fn family_ordinal(name: string) -> int { [f.ordinal for f in Family.all() if f.name == name][0] }

fn methods_ordinal() -> int { family_ordinal("Methods") }

/// `a` declares `f`; `b` calls it; `c` lives in a module of its own and names neither.
fn package_files() -> Map<string, string> {
    {
        "/w/src/a.av": "export fn f() -> int {\n    1\n}\n",
        "/w/src/b.av": "export fn g() -> int {\n    f() + 1\n}\n",
        "/w/src/other/c.av": "export fn h() -> int {\n    2\n}\n",
    }
}

fn package_names() -> List<string> { ["/w/src/a.av", "/w/src/b.av", "/w/src/other/c.av"] }

/// One process's own workspace over the given files, each admitted up front, so a
/// cross-file signature always finds its callee's declaration minted.
fn a_process_over(files: Map<string, string>, names: List<string>) -> Workspace {
    let ws = test_workspace(memory_host(files, names), "/w")
    for path in names { let _ = ws.items(ws.file_id(path)) }
    ws
}

/// A file checked in `ws` as `avra check` checks it — its analysis and its rule
/// findings — answering whether it is clean.
fn checked(ws: Workspace, path: string) -> bool {
    let a = ws.analysis(ws.file_id(path))
    let _ = rule_findings(analysed(a), a.view.stmts)
    a.clean()
}

/// The declaration named `name` that `file` declares.
fn decl_in_file(ws: Workspace, file: string, name: string) -> DeclId {
    [d.id for d in ws.decls.all_decls() if d.name == name && ws.decls.file(d.file).path == file][0]
}

// A BODY'S TYPED ANSWER IS ITS OWN: the program layer types each item on its own tape, its nodes
// counted from where the declaration starts, so a declaration written above it leaves what typing
// found standing, and a change to its own body moves it. Read as the rules read it: the item's
// typed facts (`RuleFacts.Typed`), each node's type spelled.
use @std.avrac.testing.{judged}
use features.{RuleFacts}

fn td_body(n: string) -> string { "fn b(x: int) -> int {\n    let y = x + ${n}\n    y * 2\n}\n\nb(1)\n" }

/// What typing found in `b`'s item, in a program of `text`: each node's type, by its index.
fn td_digest(text: string) -> string {
    let items = judged(text).rule_items("/alone/src/main.av")
    let item? = items.find((i) -> i.stmts.any((s) -> i.file.view.store.declared_name(s) == "b")) else { return "no item" }
    match item.file.facts {
        .Typed(t) -> [t2?.spelled() ?? "_" for t2 in t.types].join(","),
        .Analysed(_) -> "old facts",
    }
}

spec "compiler/typed digest — a body's digest is its own" {
    given "a declaration written above `b`" {
        then "b's typed digest stands" {
            td_digest(td_body("1")) == td_digest("fn above(a: int) -> int {\n    a + a * 3\n}\n\n${td_body("1")}")
        }
    }
    given "a change to b's own body" {
        then "b's typed digest moves" { td_digest(td_body("1")) != td_digest(td_body("\"s\".length")) }
    }
    given "any program" {
        then "b's item is typed at all" { td_digest(td_body("1")).contains("int") }
    }
}
EOF

#!/bin/sh
# ONE FIXTURE OF THE SOUNDNESS SWEEP: the old `check` (net on), then the layer's `build` (net off),
# each bounded at 300 s; one TSV line on stdout:
#   path  old_exit  old_first  old_first_error  layer_exit  layer_first  layer_first_error
# where `first` is the first diagnostic as `error:kind` or `warning:kind`. The fixture's build
# products (`.avra-cache`) are deleted after, so a sweep never fills the disk.
# usage: one.sh <tree at d00e7c64, built> <out dir for logs> <fixture path relative to the tree>
tree=$1; out=$2; rel=$3; cd "$tree" || exit 0
mkdir -p "$out"
key=$(printf '%s' "$rel" | tr '/' '_')
first() { grep -m1 -oE '^(error|warning)\[[^]]+\]' "$1" | sed -E 's/^(error|warning)\[(.*)\]$/\1:\2/'; }
firsterr() { grep -m1 -oE '^error\[[^]]+\]' "$1" | sed -E 's/^error\[(.*)\]$/\1/'; }
AVRA_PROGRAM=0 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=1 timeout 300 build/avra check "$rel" > "$out/$key.old" 2>&1; oe=$?
AVRA_PROGRAM=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 timeout 300 build/avra build "$rel" > "$out/$key.new" 2>&1; ne=$?
d=$rel; [ -d "$d" ] || d=$(dirname "$rel")
find "$d" -path '*/.avra-cache/*' -delete 2>/dev/null; find "$d" -name .avra-cache -type d -empty -delete 2>/dev/null
printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$rel" "$oe" "$(first $out/$key.old)" "$(firsterr $out/$key.old)" "$ne" "$(first $out/$key.new)" "$(firsterr $out/$key.new)"
EOF

# The program layer's refusal suite

Each directory here is a package of its own, one case: a source the program layer must refuse
in the old path's words, or must build. `sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh` judges them all;
its head says what each file means. In short:

- `refuses.expected`: the old path's `avra check` words, its warnings aside, paths as `<case>`.
  Both the old `check` and `AVRA_PROGRAM=1 avra build` exit 1 saying exactly this.
- `prints.expected`: what the product prints. The old `check` exits 0, the program layer builds
  the package, and its binary prints exactly this.
- `differs.why`: the paths are known to differ here, for the reason on its first line. The case
  is said and not failed while it differs, and fails once it holds until the file goes.
  `sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --known` lists them.

A new case is a directory with `avra.toml` and `src/main.av`; `PIN=1 sh
tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra-try <case>` gives it the old path's expectation.

WHY HERE AND NOT UNDER A PACKAGE'S `src/`: `avra test` builds every package nested under a
package's sources as a suite of its own (`nested_roots` in compiler/suite.av), so a case that must
be refused would fail that package's tests. Under `tools/` no suite reaches them, as with
`tools/wasm-refuses/`.
